training-data.name: Training Data
training-data.description: The clean demonstrations, labels, preference pairs and corpora a model is trained or fine-tuned on.

benchmark-data.name: Benchmark Data
benchmark-data.description: Ground-truth evaluation sets, answer keys and baseline traffic used to measure whether an attack or defense really works.

trusted-documents.name: Trusted Documents
trusted-documents.description: Knowledge bases, emails, tool results, task data and other content an application or agent reads as legitimate context.

victim-tenant.name: Victim Tenant
victim-tenant.description: The user or tenant whose data, prefix or session ends up exposed to another party on shared infrastructure.

model-file.name: Model File
model-file.description: The serialized checkpoint, adapter or tensor bytes that sit on disk before a loader turns them into a running model.

poisoned-data.name: Poisoned Data
poisoned-data.description: Attacker-planted, triggered or leaked training rows that change what a model learns.

prompt-injection.name: Prompt Injection
prompt-injection.description: Instructions an attacker types straight into the prompt to override the operator's intent or extract what should stay hidden.

indirect-injection.name: Indirect Injection
indirect-injection.description: Hidden instructions planted in pages, emails, images, tool descriptions or tool output that an agent later reads and obeys.

retrieval-poisoning.name: Retrieval Poisoning
retrieval-poisoning.description: Planted or unauthorized documents that get into a retrieval index and so into the model's context.

adversarial-perturbation.name: Adversarial Perturbation
adversarial-perturbation.description: Gradient-guided pixel noise or token suffixes that push a model toward an attacker-chosen output.

tampered-artifact.name: Tampered Artifact
tampered-artifact.description: A swapped adapter, edited tensor, injected pickle opcode, rewritten template or altered code that gets in through the model supply chain.

extraction-probe.name: Extraction Probe
extraction-probe.description: Attacker queries and measurements that steal a model or infer private facts such as membership, hidden size or another tenant's prompt.

leak-path.name: Leak Path
leak-path.description: The route that carries a secret, a memorized record or another tenant's data out to someone who should not see it.

resource-abuse.name: Resource Abuse
resource-abuse.description: Inputs or settings an attacker chooses to drive up compute, tokens or server load.

guardrail-bypass.name: Guardrail Bypass
guardrail-bypass.description: Ways to slip harmful input past a detector, filter or text-only control without tripping it.

attack-surface.name: Exposed Attack Surface
attack-surface.description: Endpoints, tool arguments and defaults that are open or unchecked unless someone locks them down.

model-weights.name: Model Weights
model-weights.description: The learned parameters (full weights, adapters, soft prompts, UNets) that decide what a model is.

model-internals.name: Model Internals
model-internals.description: Activations, attention heads, embeddings, logits, scores and control tokens inside a forward pass.

training-pipeline.name: Training Pipeline
training-pipeline.description: The training, fine-tuning, reward-model or preference-optimization process that turns data into weights.

model-loader.name: Model Loader
model-loader.description: The deserializer, template renderer or repo code that runs when a model file is opened.

inference-server.name: Inference Server
inference-server.description: The serving runtime, with its slots, prompt and KV caches and shared state across requests.

llm-agent.name: LLM Agent
llm-agent.description: An assistant or group of agents that holds credentials, memory and tools on a user's behalf.

retrieval.name: Retrieval Pipeline
retrieval.description: The embedder, vector index and ranked context that a RAG system puts in front of the model.

classifier-guard.name: Classifier / Judge
classifier-guard.description: A detector, filter model or LLM judge whose verdict decides what passes or how something is scored.

downstream-sink.name: Downstream Sink
downstream-sink.description: Tools, runners, peer agents and interpreters that act on model output and so turn text into consequences.

measurement.name: Measurement
measurement.description: Scores, accuracies, timings and verdicts used to tell whether an attack succeeded.

provenance-check.name: Provenance & Pinning
provenance-check.description: Defenses that pin hashes, sign manifests and trace lineage so a swapped or edited artifact is refused.

behavior-gate.name: Behavior Gate
behavior-gate.description: Release gates that rerun held-out probes and refuse a model or adapter that misbehaves.

data-audit.name: Data Audit
data-audit.description: Defenses that scan, deduplicate, cluster or quarantine training data before and after training.

safe-loading.name: Safe Loading
safe-loading.description: Allowlist loaders, data-only formats and sandboxed parsing that stop a model file from running code.

input-filter.name: Input Filter
input-filter.description: Classifiers, normalization, perplexity checks and screens that inspect input before the model acts on it.

output-filter.name: Output Filter
output-filter.description: Validation and encoding applied to model output before it is shown or executed.

access-control.name: Access Control
access-control.description: Authentication, scoped tokens, authorization-aware retrieval and least privilege that limit who can reach what.

tenant-isolation.name: Tenant Isolation
tenant-isolation.description: Per-tenant cache salts, session binding and partitioning that keep one customer's state away from another's.

resource-limits.name: Resource Limits
resource-limits.description: Token caps, step budgets, rate limits and cost monitoring that bound how much work one request can trigger.

output-minimization.name: Minimal API Output
output-minimization.description: Returning labels instead of scores, rounding and truncating so an API gives away less to extraction.

robust-training.name: Robust Training
robust-training.description: Adversarial training, DP-SGD and regularization that make a model harder to fool or to mine for data.

prompt-hardening.name: Prompt Hardening
prompt-hardening.description: Instruction hierarchy, delimiting, spotlighting and system-prompt rules that tell a model to treat content as data.

action-approval.name: Action Approval
action-approval.description: Typed channels, bound approvals and gated executors that keep an agent's consequential actions under control.

evaluation-rigor.name: Evaluation Rigor
evaluation-rigor.description: Fresh splits, reference checks and honest success counting so a reported number means what it claims.

server-side-policy.name: Server-Side Policy
server-side-policy.description: Fixing decoding settings, templates, stop rules and allowed input types on the server instead of trusting the client.
